name: Lexiscript Consent & Privacy
author: jmwatee

sections.description:
Most consent banners describe what a site does. This one changes it.

The Lexiscript widget intercepts the browser APIs that scripts use to insert themselves, so a
tracker is caught at the moment it tries to load rather than disclosed after it has already run.
Non-essential scripts do not execute until the visitor has agreed — and what counts as agreement
depends on where that visitor is.

Region-aware by default. A visitor in Germany, one in California and one in Kenya get
different behaviour from the same installation. The widget applies one of three consent models
according to the visitor’s location:

  • Opt-in, where nothing runs until consent is given: EU, UK, Kenya, Nigeria, Brazil
  • Opt-out, presented as “Do Not Sell or Share”: California
  • Notice-only: South Africa, Canada

These groupings reflect how Lexiscript reads the published rules for each region. They are a
product configuration, not a legal determination about your site — see “Not legal advice” below.

What the widget does on your site

  • Blocks non-essential scripts before they run, rather than describing them afterwards
  • Shows a preference centre with per-category choices, not all-or-nothing
  • Gives “Reject all” the same prominence as “Accept”
  • Pre-ticks nothing under an opt-in model
  • Honours the Global Privacy Control signal automatically
  • Treats a stored decision as expired after the configured lifetime
  • Invalidates previous consent when the tracker set changes, because the visitor never agreed
    to the new ones
  • Never blocks the page itself — the scripts are blocked, not your content
  • Fails closed: if the configuration cannot be reached, it serves deny-all rather than letting
    everything through
  • One small vanilla JavaScript file, no framework, no dependencies

Why this plugin exists

The widget is one script, and the only thing that is easy to get wrong is where it goes — it must
run before every other script on the page or it has nothing left to intercept. This plugin
registers it with WordPress’s script loader and prints it at the top of the document head, ahead
of the tags that themes and other plugins add, and keeps it there through theme changes.

Plans and pricing

A Lexiscript account is free, and so is scanning your site and reading the findings. The
consent widget that this plugin installs requires a paid plan. Without one, your site key will
not return a widget configuration and no banner will appear.

Current pricing is on https://jaytechkenya.com/lexiscript. Nothing in this plugin stops working
after a trial — the widget is a paid feature from the start, and the plugin tells you so on its
settings screen before you enter anything.

External service

This plugin requires a Lexiscript account and loads a script from Lexiscript, a service operated
by Jaydee Innovation Hub (Nairobi, Kenya). The plugin does not function without it.

  • The plugin registers and prints one script, served from https://widget.jaytechkenya.com,
    with your site key as a query parameter. This is Lexiscript’s own service endpoint, not a
    general-purpose third-party CDN, and the script is the service.
  • That script runs in your visitors’ browsers. It requests your site’s consent configuration
    from Lexiscript, and the visitor’s IP address is used at the edge to resolve their country —
    and US state where relevant — in order to decide which consent model applies. The IP address
    is used for that lookup and is not retained as part of a visitor profile.
  • The visitor’s own consent choices are stored in their browser. They are not sent to
    Lexiscript.
  • This plugin itself makes no requests to Lexiscript from your server, and reads or transmits
    nothing from your WordPress database.
  • Service terms: https://jaytechkenya.com/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://jaytechkenya.com/privacy
  • About the service: https://jaytechkenya.com/lexiscript

Not legal advice

Lexiscript reports what your website does and which published rules are relevant to it. It does
not determine whether your site is lawful, it does not make your site compliant with any law,
and nothing it produces is legal advice. Whether your use of this plugin meets your obligations
is a question for your own adviser.
sections.installation:
1. Create an account at https://jaytechkenya.com/lexiscript and add your website.
  2. Open your website in the Lexiscript dashboard and copy the id from the install snippet.
  3. Install and activate this plugin.
  4. Go to Settings → Lexiscript and paste the id into the Site key field.
  5. Load your site in a private window. The banner should appear, and your analytics should not
    fire until you accept.

If the banner does not appear, check that your Lexiscript plan includes the consent widget.

If you previously pasted the Lexiscript tag into your theme by hand, remove it — two copies of
the widget is not better than one.
sections.faq:
Do I need a paid plan?

For the consent widget, yes. Creating an account, adding a website and scanning it are free, and
that is enough to see what your site is doing. Serving the widget to visitors is a paid feature.

Why does this script load before everything else?

Because it has to. The widget works by intercepting the browser APIs that scripts use to insert
themselves, which only affects scripts that load after it. The plugin registers the widget with
wp_register_script() and then prints that one handle at wp_head priority 0, rather than
letting it print with the rest of the queue at priority 9 — several tag-manager plugins
deliberately hook earlier than 9, and anything that loads first wins.

It is not blocking my Google Tag Manager container

Check that no other plugin or your theme is printing a tag above this one. This plugin prints at
wp_head priority 0, which is earlier than anything using the default priority, but code hooked
at priority 0 before it, or hard-coded directly into header.php above wp_head(), will still
win. Move it below wp_head() and it will be caught.

Will this slow my site down?

The widget is a single small JavaScript file. It is loaded synchronously and deliberately so: a
deferred or asynchronous script cannot intercept tags that have already started loading, which
would defeat the point.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. The tag is static markup, so it caches like the rest of the page. The consent decision
itself is made in the visitor’s browser, not on your server, so a cached page serves the correct
behaviour to every visitor regardless of where they are.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Each site in the network has its own site key, set on that site’s own settings screen.

Can I point it at a different host?

Yes, for self-hosted or staging deployments, by defining a constant in wp-config.php:

define( 'LEXISCRIPT_WIDGET_HOST', 'https://widget.example.com' );

It is deliberately not a setting. The value decides the origin of a script that runs on every
page of your site, so it belongs with your deployment constants rather than in a form.

What happens if I deactivate it?

The tag stops being printed and trackers run as they did before. Your settings are kept in case
you reactivate; deleting the plugin removes them.
